text: 中国人民银行主管的《金融时报》发文称，电影《牛来》8月5日上映，9天累计票房仅7169元、总观影236人次，几乎没什么人知道。然而，凭借粗糙到抽象的建模和有些荒诞的剧情，影片靠“烂得出奇”在社交平台反向出圈，又因片名读起来顺口讨喜，被部分股民赋予了特殊寓意。事实上，A股历史上类似的“名字行情”并不少见。每逢热点事件，名称沾边的个股总会被资金短暂“关照”一番，但行情往往来得快去得也快。从早年的“情人节概念股”，到重大事件期间名称谐音的个股异动，再到各种“概念加持”下的无厘头涨停，类似戏码反复出现，其共同特征是起因牵强附会、逻辑经不起推敲、资金快进快出、行情
text_en: The Financial News, under the People's Bank of China, reported that the film 'Niu Lai,' released on August 5, grossed only 7,169 yuan over nine days with 236 total viewings, barely noticed by anyone. However, thanks to crudely abstract modeling and absurd plot, the film went viral in reverse on social media for being 'astonishingly bad,' and its catchy, auspicious-sounding title led some retail investors to赋予 it special meaning. In fact, similar 'name-driven' market moves are not uncommon in A-share history. Whenever a hot event occurs, stocks with related names tend to get brief attention from capital, but such moves often come and go quickly. From early 'Valentine's Day concept stocks' to homophone stock anomalies during major events, and then to nonsensical limit-ups under various 'concept boosts,' similar scenarios repeat—characterized by far-fetched causes, shaky logic, fast in-and-out capital, and fleeting trends.
